subject: Streamline consumer-facing console copy for DPA/subprocessor & cross-border notes
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sophie Mann <sophie@elevatelegal.com>, Acme Cloud Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Console copy: short, consumer-friendly DPA/subprocessor + cross-border blurb

Hi all —

We need a focused, customer-facing update for the Console that clearly explains: (1) why we list subprocessors, (2) how data may move cross-border for hosted API, and (3) what controls customers have (residency toggle / Dedicated / Private). Acme has flagged the current text as "too legal / too dense" and security asked for a short FAQ and an expand/collapse tooltip.

Attached: dpa_redline_v2.docx (legal redlines) and subprocessor_matrix.csv (current list).

Asks:
- Kimberly: quick legal-safe 2–3 sentence blurb we can show inline in the Console; and a 1-line tooltip for the DPA modal.
- Laura & Vanessa: product/UX take — can we fit a 200–250 char summary plus a clickable "see details" with the full subprocessor list? Any constraints for the tooltip length?
- Sophie / Acme Security: any specific phrasing you'd prefer for customers in regulated industries?

Goal: ship a Console copy refresh for hosted API customers and a variant for Sales one-pager by EOD Thursday.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Mann <sophie@elevatelegal.com>, Acme Cloud Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Console copy: short, consumer-friendly DPA/subprocessor + cross-border blurb

Irene — quick pass from legal below. Keeping it short but accurate is the right call. Two versions: "teaser" (for inline) and "tooltip" (one-liner).

Inline (approx. 220 chars):
"Redwood lists third-party subprocessors we use to provide inference services. We may transfer data across jurisdictions to operate the service; customers can choose Dedicated or Private deployment for residency and isolation controls. See full DPA for details and opt-out options."

Tooltip (tooltip-length, ~120 chars):
"We use subprocessors to operate the service. Learn how data moves and residency options in the DPA."

Notes / legal caveats:
- Avoid absolutes like "never" or "won't" re: transfers — keep conditional language.
- If we say "opt-out," ensure the console links to the procurement path (procurement contact + form).
- The subprocessor CSV should be surfaced as a live list (not a static PDF) so customers can confirm current vendors.

I attached minor redlines in dpa_redline_v2.docx; I recommend we publish the blurb and link to the live list + DPA.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Mann <sophie@elevatelegal.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Cloud Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Console copy: short, consumer-friendly DPA/subprocessor + cross-border blurb

Thanks — Kim's drafts look good. A few customer-facing tweaks that help reduce questions from procurement/security teams: use "how we use subprocessors" framing and add a short "what you can do" bullet set. Sample layout below:

[Console snippet — display block]
Heading: "Third-party subprocessors & data movement"
Summary (1–2 lines): "We work with third parties to run our service. Some processing may occur outside your region depending on hosting and model runtime."
Bullets (3 short bullets):
- "Where your data can stay: Choose Dedicated or Private deployments for guaranteed residency."
- "Current vendors: View the live subprocessor list (updates automatically)."
- "Need an exception? Contact procurement@redwood.ai for residency or data handling requests."
Link: "Read the DPA and transfer terms" (opens modal with details + redline link).

Also consider a short FAQ modal with answers to: "Why do you publish subprocessors?" and "Does Redwood sell customer data?" — brief, plain answers mitigate RFP churn.

Happy to iterate on the exact phrasing if you want client-ready language for Acme.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Mann
Elevate Legal (external counsel)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Mann <sophie@elevatelegal.com>, Acme Cloud Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Console copy: short, consumer-friendly DPA/subprocessor + cross-border blurb

Thanks — product / UX notes below. TL;DR: can do inline 200–220 char summary + a modal with live list + FAQ. Tooltip must be proofed for truncation at 140 chars.

UX constraints / proposals:
- Inline summary location: beneath "Data handling" section on Account Settings (near residency toggle).
- Modal: 3 tabs — (1) Summary + one-line legal blurb, (2) Live subprocessor list (table pulled from subprocessor_matrix.csv), (3) FAQ (3–5 Qs).
- CTA: "Request residency exception" (linked to procurement form).

Copy prefs: use Sophie's heading + Kim's inline sentence, trimmed as: "We use third parties to run the service. Processing may occur outside your region; Dedicated/Private deployments preserve residency." (200 chars).

Accessibility / i18n note: tooltip and modal copy should be short for translation quality. Laura will provide the exact 200-char variant by EOB 3/15. Vanessa — can you confirm engineering timeline for the live list (read-only endpoint) and whether we can show "last updated"?

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sophie Mann <sophie@elevatelegal.com>, Acme Cloud Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Console copy: short, consumer-friendly DPA/subprocessor + cross-border blurb

Appreciate the fast turn. Quick summary of decisions and next steps: 

1) Copy approved for initial rollout (console + sales snippet):
- Inline summary (200 chars): "We use third parties to run the service. Processing may occur outside your region; Dedicated or Private deployments let you preserve data residency and isolation."
- Tooltip (120 chars): "We use subprocessors to operate the service. See DPA for transfer details and residency options."

2) Modal & live list: Laura to deliver modal copy (final) by 3/15 EOB; Vanessa to confirm read-only endpoint and "last updated" flag by 3/16 EOD.

3) Legal: Kimberly to publish the two-sentence blurb in the DPA modal and add a procurement contact line (procurement@redwood.ai). She will finalize redlines in dpa_redline_v2.docx and confirm we can surface the live CSV link.

4) External counsel / customer: Sophie & Acme — if the above is acceptable, we'll share a staging link for Acme to review on 3/17.

If no objections, I'll ask Docs + Engineering to schedule the console update for the next minor release.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: final legal blurb + confirm live list linkage (due 3/16 5pm PT)
- Laura: final 200-char copy for translation (due 3/15 EOB)
- Vanessa: endpoint + last-updated field confirmation (due 3/16 EOD)
- Sophie / Acme: quick read & thumbs up on the staging link (target 3/17)

Thanks everyone —
Irene
